metadata.title: High fever and severe body aches during monsoon season in Lahore
metadata.author: seed

patient.name: Ayesha Siddiqui
patient.communication_style: Cooperative, winces with the body pain

history.chief_complaint: Sudden high fever with terrible body and eye pain for 3 days

history_of_presenting_illness.pain: Severe muscle and joint aches; pain behind the eyes
history_of_presenting_illness.rash: A faint blanching rash appeared on the arms and chest today
history_of_presenting_illness.bleeding: Mild gum bleeding when brushing teeth; no black stools
history_of_presenting_illness.context: Several neighbours have dengue; standing rainwater near the house

social_history: Lives in Lahore during monsoon season

general_skin.rash: Blanching macular rash on the trunk and limbs

laboratory.name: Complete Blood Count
laboratory.clinical_significance: Key for dengue diagnosis and monitoring for plasma leakage

laboratory.name: Dengue NS1 Antigen
laboratory.clinical_significance: Useful in the first few days of illness

imaging.name: Chest X-Ray
imaging.clinical_significance: May show pleural effusion if plasma leakage develops

bedside.name: Malaria Rapid Diagnostic Test
bedside.clinical_significance: Reasonable to exclude malaria as a co-endemic febrile illness

diagnosis.explanation: Abrupt high fever with severe myalgia, retro-orbital pain, a blanching rash and positive tourniquet test during a monsoon outbreak, with thrombocytopenia, rising haematocrit and a positive NS1 antigen, confirms dengue fever.

emergency_management: Assess for dengue warning signs and plasma-leakage/shock
Careful oral or IV fluid management; monitor haematocrit and platelets
Paracetamol for fever — AVOID NSAIDs and aspirin (bleeding risk)
definitive_management: Supportive care; escalate fluids per haematocrit if leakage develops
follow_up: Daily review during the critical phase (days 4-6)
patient_education: Return immediately with abdominal pain, bleeding, or lethargy

items.description: Elicited classic dengue features (retro-orbital pain, myalgia, rash)
Fluid management and serial CBC monitoring

pearls: NSAIDs and aspirin are contraindicated in dengue — use paracetamol.
The critical (plasma-leakage) phase is around days 4-6 as the fever settles.
pitfalls: Over- or under-hydration; not tracking serial haematocrit and platelets.
Missing warning signs that herald severe dengue.
references: WHO Dengue guidelines; Punjab dengue protocols
learning_objectives: Recognise dengue and its warning signs.
